predecessors.name: Portuguese Empire
predecessors.text: the Portuguese dependencies in the Lesser Sunda Islands from Lifau: Timor as far as the final border, with the Larantuka-Solor-Adonara cluster and Sikka

successors.name: East Timor
successors.text: the colony in its final borders (infobox area 14,874 km2)

ledger.x: 1702: Portugal's Timor colony begins at Lifau.
1769: the capital moves from Lifau to Dili (infobox 'Lifau (1702-69)'; 'Dili (1769-1942; 1945-75)').
20 April 1859: Portugal gives up the Flores cluster.
20 April 1859: Portugal receives Maubara and Ambeno.

wars.name: Battle of Timor
wars.outcome: Japan invaded in February 1942 and occupied the colony until 1945 while 400 Australian and Dutch commandos fought a guerrilla campaign.

wars.name: Indonesian invasion of East Timor
wars.outcome: On 7 December 1975 Indonesian forces invaded, nine days after Fretilin's declaration of 28 November; the Portuguese colony had ceased to administer the territory by then.

certainty.note: The page gives no extent; Portuguese authority outside the coast and the capital was thin, and the 'dependencies' were kingdoms (liurai) under Topasses and Dominicans.

The treaty of 20 April 1859 'establishes the boundaries' on Timor, the 1904 treaty exchanged enclaves and 'The definitive border was established by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 1914 and ratified in 1916'.
